device.category: six-operator FM synthesizer and MIDI controller

audio_outputs.name: headphone output
audio_outputs.purpose: headphones or connection to a mixer or audio interface
audio_outputs.speaker_behavior: connecting headphones mutes the internal speaker

usb_audio.note: The manual documents USB as MIDI; do not plan on USB audio without an observed test.

documented_behavior: USB-C MIDI, BLE MIDI, and 3.5 mm MIDI input are documented as simultaneously active.
The FM-1 receives notes with velocity, pitch bend, CC, and supported FM SysEx.
Keyboard, arpeggiator, and sequencer notes transmit over USB MIDI and BLE MIDI on the configured note channel.
The 3.5 mm MIDI connector is input only.

performance_and_control.polyphony: Mono or Poly mode; up to 12 voices in Poly mode
performance_and_control.preset_memory: 128 factory presets; edited presets can be saved to flash
clocked_features: arpeggiator and sequencer cannot be active together

power.battery: internal 2000 mAh battery; vendor product data states approximately 12 hours

connection_rules.rule: To hear FM-1 in a PA, mixer, or audio interface, use its 3.5 mm stereo audio output. USB-C MIDI, BLE MIDI, and 3.5 mm MIDI IN do not replace the audio connection.
The manual documents its 3.5 mm MIDI connector as MIDI IN. Do not plan a direct physical MIDI-out cable from FM-1 to an XPS-30 or other hardware synthesizer.
For USB or BLE control of another hardware synthesizer, use a computer, mobile host, or documented MIDI-host interface that can receive FM-1 MIDI and send it to the target's MIDI IN.

roles: USB or BLE MIDI keyboard/controller for a host
hardware FM module controlled through 3.5 mm MIDI IN
sequenced or arpeggiated auxiliary sound source with separate audio routing
unknowns: The stored manual does not document a USB-audio interface. Verify actual Linux endpoints before claiming USB audio support.
Record the required 3.5 mm MIDI adapter wiring before connecting an external MIDI source.
